correctness.rationale: Every hypothesis and boundary is explicit: ordinary H(n)=n(2n-1), n>=2, gcd of triple one and minimal embedding dimension three except n=3. Exact formulas gcd(a,b), gcd(b,c), gcd(a,c) bound pairwise gcd by 30. If a>d(c-a), the gluing relation forces s+t=d; the only midpoint possibility would require 8n+6|d, impossible. Hence n>=122 excluded by the strictly increasing polynomial 2n²-241n-180>0. For n<=121, exact gcd restrictions yield 24 pair/index candidates. An invertible coefficient modulo y gives a necessary-and-sufficient nonnegative two-generator membership test; the complete 24-residue table leaves n=2,3,6,7,8,18. n=3 is directly two-generated. All six Frobenius values follow from Fel §2 symmetric-triple formula or Sylvester two-generator formula, and genera from g=(F+1)/2. The actual packaged exact verifier independently computes Apéry sets and genus for all 120 indices, with no floating point. Finite checks corroborate but do not replace the n>=122 proof.

The complete OEIS A069758 entry (2002) does not give symmetry indices/genus. value.rationale: A complete iff classification of a natural and historically tabulated family of 3-generated numerical semigroups is a motivated invariant problem: semigroup symmetry is equivalent to the sharp genus/Frobenius equality and 3-generator complete intersection. The six exceptional indices, especially the isolated n=18 case, are mathematically structured and not a mere table recitation. The novel gcd support and uniform cutoff reduce an infinite question to only 24 auditable modular tests, sharpening general finite-boundedness to the exact last exceptional index. The theorem excludes all other n and reports the associated natural invariants; no unrelated arbitrary restriction or unsupported downstream application is asserted.
